chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Will you not inform me from where you knew and said that the wiping is with part of the head and part of the two feet?' So he smiled and said: 'O Zurara! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said so and the Book was revealed with it from Allah, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Wash your faces', thus we recognized that the entire face ought to be washed.

Then He said: 'and your hands as far as the elbows'. Then He detailed between the speech, so He said: 'and wipe your heads'. So we recognized when He said 'your heads' that the wiping is with part of the head due to the placement of the letter 'Ba'.

Then He linked the two feet with the head just as He linked the two hands with the face, so He said: 'and your feet to the ankles'. Thus, we recognized when He linked it with the head that the wiping is upon part of it.
Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) interpreted that for the people, but they neglected it.

Then He said: 'and if you do not find water, then betake yourselves to pure earth and wipe your faces and your hands from it'. So when the Wudu was established, if you do not find water, it affirmed part of the washing as wiping, because He said 'wipe your faces', then He linked with it 'and your hands'.

Then He said 'from it', i.e., from that Tayammum, because He knew that that is more comprehensive. It did not proceed upon the face entirely, because he attaches from that earth with part of the palm, and does not attach with part of it.
Then He said: 'Allah does not intend to put upon you any difficulty in the religion', and the difficulty is the narrowness.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic evidence for wiping part of the head and feet during Wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Zurara queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on the jurisprudential basis for partial wiping (*masah*) of the head and feet, a key distinction in Shia fiqh. The Imam elucidates that the grammatical structure of Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:6), specifically the preposition 'Ba' and the syntactic linkage (*'atf*) of the feet to the head, indicates partiality rather than full washing. He further reinforces this by analyzing the verse of Tayammum, where the partial wiping of the face and hands from dust establishes a precedent for the same method applied to the limbs in Wudu.
